meta.description: WhatsApp accepts videos up to 2 GB when sent as a document. Sent from the gallery, videos are limited to about 16 MB in most regions and recompressed hard. See how much video fits in 16 MB and compress yours first, on your own device.
og.title: WhatsApp video size limit: 2 GB as a document, 16 MB as media
og.description: Send as a document for 2 GB, or compress to 16 MB so it plays inline without WhatsApp blurring it.
hero.title: WhatsApp video size limit
hero.lead: WhatsApp takes videos up to 2 GB — but only when you send them as a document. Sent the normal way, from the gallery or camera roll, the limit is about 16 MB in most regions and WhatsApp recompresses the video on your phone, which is where the blur comes from. Compressing it yourself first avoids both problems.
qa.h2: WhatsApp video limits at a glance
qa.r3.v: Limited by length rather than size — the app trims a longer video into pieces before posting.
qa.after: So there are really two limits. A document goes through untouched at any size up to 2 GB, but the recipient has to download and open it. A media send previews and plays inline in the chat, but has to be small — and if you let WhatsApp do the shrinking, it uses one-size-fits-all settings that leave the video smeared.
tool.h2: Compress your video to 16 MB before sending
tool.lead: Drop the video below. It is compressed to just under 16 MB on your own device — nothing is uploaded — using settings chosen for this clip, so WhatsApp has no reason to recompress it again. The output is a standard MP4 that plays inline on iPhone and Android.
fit.h2: How much video fits in 16 MB?
fit.lead: Length is what decides it: the same 16 MB is spread across every second, so a longer video gets a smaller picture. These rows are what this compressor actually produces from a typical phone recording — full HD, 30 frames a second, with sound.
fit.caption: What 16 MB gives you at different video lengths
fit.r1.q: Full HD — hard to tell from the original
fit.r3.q: Reduced size — looks fine on a phone, which is where WhatsApp video is watched
fit.r4.q: Small picture; watchable in the chat, blocky on a big screen
fit.after: Past about 22 minutes, 16 MB is no longer enough for a picture worth watching. For a video that long, send it as a document — it goes through at full quality up to 2 GB — or let the compressor keep the opening stretch that fits, which it offers automatically when a clip is too long.
over.h2: Sending a long video on WhatsApp without ruining it
over.p1: The document route is the one most people don't know about. In the chat, tap the attach icon, choose Document rather than Gallery, and pick the video file. WhatsApp sends it exactly as it is, up to 2 GB, with no recompression — the trade-off is that it shows as a file to download rather than a video that plays in place.
over.p2: For anything you want playing inline, compress here first. It runs locally in your browser — the video never leaves your device — and the result stays under 16 MB with the quality budget spent where it matters. If the file is already small, WhatsApp still recompresses media sends slightly, but a well-encoded input gives it far less to destroy.
faq.q1: What is WhatsApp's actual video size limit?
faq.a1: Two numbers: 2 GB per file when sent as a document, and about 16 MB when sent as media from the gallery (some regions and app versions allow more). Media sends also get recompressed by WhatsApp; document sends don't.
faq.q2: Why does my video look blurry after sending it on WhatsApp?
faq.a2: Because WhatsApp recompresses every media send on your phone with fixed, aggressive settings. Compressing the video yourself to under 16 MB first — with settings chosen for that clip — gives WhatsApp far less reason to crush it, and the result looks intentional rather than mangled.
faq.q3: How long can a WhatsApp video be?
faq.a3: For chats, WhatsApp limits size rather than length: at 16 MB a minute of video stays sharp and about 20 minutes is the practical ceiling at a small picture size. Sent as a document, length doesn't matter up to 2 GB. Status videos are cut into segments by the app.
faq.q4: Should I send my video as a document or as media?
faq.a4: As media if you want it to preview and play inline in the chat — compress it to under 16 MB first so it looks good. As a document if quality matters more than convenience, or the video is long: it arrives untouched, but the recipient downloads and opens it like a file.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded anywhere when I compress it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. Only the finished file goes to WhatsApp, and only when you send it.
